part.text: I'll search for the view named "长期记忆评测" in the ArchGraph intent graph.

input.cypher: MATCH (v:View {graphKey: $graphKey}) WHERE v.name CONTAINS '长期记忆评测' RETURN v.id, v.name
MATCH (v:View {graphKey: $graphKey}) WHERE v.name CONTAINS '记忆' RETURN v.id, v.name

part.text: No results. Let me search more broadly for any view containing part of the name.

input.cypher: MATCH (v:View {graphKey: $graphKey}) WHERE v.name CONTAINS '评测' RETURN v.id, v.name
MATCH (v) WHERE v.graphKey = $graphKey AND (v.name CONTAINS '记忆' OR v.name CONTAINS '评测' OR toLower(v.name) CONTAINS 'memory') RETURN labels(v) AS labels, v.id, v.name LIMIT 50

part.text: No views matching. Let me check how views are stored in the graph to make sure I'm querying the right structure.

input.cypher: MATCH (v) WHERE v.graphKey = $graphKey RETURN DISTINCT labels(v) AS labels, count(*) AS c

part.text: The Views are labeled `View`. My earlier query used a property `v.name` with CONTAINS '记忆' on `View` labels and got 0. But there are 40 View nodes. Let me query the View names to check exact naming (maybe stored differently).

input.cypher: MATCH (v:View) WHERE v.graphKey = $graphKey RETURN keys(v) LIMIT 1

part.text: The View nodes have null id and name in Neo4j projection. The view names are stored in the JSON graph instead. Let me query the graph structure to see how views store their names.

input.cypher: MATCH (v:View) WHERE v.graphKey = $graphKey RETURN properties(v) LIMIT 1

part.text: The property is `view_name`, not `name`. Let me query for the view with view_name matching our target.

input.cypher: MATCH (v:View {graphKey: $graphKey}) WHERE v.view_name CONTAINS '长期' OR v.view_name CONTAINS '记忆评测' RETURN v.view_id, v.view_name, v.parent_element_id
